claims.statement: Root pytest config excludes live and e2e tests by default (-m "not live and not e2e"), declares the live and e2e markers, uses --import-mode=importlib, measures coverage for the five workspace import packages (including langchain_chess_evals) and fails under 100%, with branch coverage enabled.
xdist parallelism (-n auto) is set in the mise test:python task rather than pytest addopts so a bare pytest stays serial for -k, --pdb and --snapshot-update.

The repo-root conftest disables LangSmith tracing (LANGSMITH_TRACING=false) unless the marker expression selects live tests, and forces plain Typer output (_TYPER_FORCE_DISABLE_TERMINAL, TERMINAL_WIDTH=200) so help output is stable under GitHub Actions.

The JS packages (apps/web, apps/review, packages/chess-ui, evals/reports) run Vitest via `vp test --run --coverage` in jsdom with v8 coverage thresholds of 100% for lines, functions, branches and statements; mise test:web runs them via `pnpm exec vp run -r test`.
apps/review writes coverage outside the app directory because `langsmith apps push` uploads the directory without reading .gitignore.

The lefthook pre-push hook runs `mise run test`; CI runs separate python (check:python, test:python, snapshot report artifact on failure), web (check:web, test:web, review:size) and e2e (Playwright Chromium install, test:e2e) jobs; neither runs live tests or the UCI smoke match.

ScriptedModel is a real BaseChatModel that replies from a script of strings, callables or exceptions, records requests, reports a provider/model for pricing, and raises AssertionError when the script is exhausted.

fake_engine writes an executable deterministic UCI engine (FakeFish 1) using the current Python interpreter that ranks moves by mate-in-one, then material, then UCI order, supports MultiPV, and with quits=False ignores `quit` to simulate a hung engine.
The chess tests' `run` fixture is parametrized over sync and async so tests exercise both invoke and ainvoke; `make_agent` defaults to an InMemorySaver checkpointer.

The server tests' env fixture clears the gateway env vars, LC_GATEWAY_KEY, OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and ALLOWED_ORGANIZATION_ID, chdirs to tmp_path to isolate from the repo .env, and sets known-good fake gateway settings.

FakeRanker returns scripted MoveDistributions (from a sequence or a callable over the request) or raises scripted errors while recording RankRequests; FakeTypeSafeClient stands in for TypeSafeClassifier and, when capped (the default, model other/ranker), enforces 2-16 options per Choice and at most 32 questions per request by raising a 422 TypeSafeAPIError.

fakeStream replaces @langchain/react's useStream via vi.mock with a mutable fake (including hydrationPromise and getThread) supporting per-thread overrides, a late-bound submit, option logging, and resetFake for cleanup.
packages/chess-ui exports a ./testing entry with overridable call, turn, ply, systemOne and live (System 1 live shortlist result) factories plus the E4_E5 fixture game and AFTER_E4 FEN.

Textual TUI snapshot tests use snap_compare for board-only cases (three sizes, piece selection, black's view with cursor, promotion dialog) and full-app cases built on a hybrid game with a ScriptedModel and FakeRanker (game screen, light theme, stepping back, game over, new-game screen, stopped turn retry, invalid advanced setting, short and narrow terminals), stubbing perf_counter for stable latencies; `pytest --snapshot-update` rewrites them.
Live tests are opt-in: they are selected only with -m live, typically via `mise run test:live` (pytest -m live --no-cov with .env), hit the real LLM Gateway and cost a few cents.

The server live tests use the shared langgraph_dev fixture and check the /ui mount via /ui/config (graph chess, default policy hybrid), a System 1 chat game with idempotent resend and illegal-move error, assistant context reaching the factory via runtime with no run config, and priced LLM calls with threshold 1.0 reporting the default model baseten:zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash.

`mise run test:uci` runs a 2-game fastchess match of `lcchess uci --policy systemone` seeds 1 vs 2 in .uci-match/ and passes only if both games have a result and no termination other than normal or adjudication.

The CI workflow runs on pull requests (ignoring Markdown, plans/** and openwiki/** changes) and is also invoked via workflow_call by the deploy and deploy-review workflows, so deployments are gated on the same checks for a given ref.

The server tests' session-scoped langgraph_dev fixture returns a factory that starts a real `langgraph dev` (--no-browser --no-reload) on a free port from a given work directory using a copy of langgraph.json with absolute graph, http.app and auth.path specs, optionally overriding the env file, process environment and graph specs, polls /ok for up to 90 s (failing with the server log if the process exits or never starts), and terminates then kills the server after 15 s.

apps/server/tests/test_server.py runs a real langgraph dev in the default (non-live) suite with fake gateway keys, tracing off and LANGSMITH_/LANGCHAIN_/TYPESAFE_/LC_ variables stripped, checking that paused runs read back with the same next/setup and graph topology via run config or assistant context, that a versioned partial override on an unversioned assistant resolves correctly, and that a hybrid run without System 1 keys errors before writing state.
langchain_chess.testing.topology returns an agent's nodes, edges and state channels, used to check that the graph the server describes matches the graph that ran.

The review app's test fixtures build a Scholar's-mate game state, a Stockfish review, gradings, game list entries, version-2 header-plus-parts reviews, and review, part and status feedback from overridable factories built on the chess-ui testing factories.

The repo-root vite.config.ts holds only lint and fmt settings because Vite+ ignores those blocks in nested configs; test configuration lives in each JS package's vite.config.ts. Its fmt ignores exclude the generated chess-ui settings files, which a test compares byte for byte.

evals/reports excludes its one-off report pages (src/experiments/**) from the coverage gate and instead has a test that globs every report, requires at least one, and checks each renders with a title and heading (30 s timeout); under test the @report alias points at a fixture report.

test_codegen compares every file from codegen.files() (settings.ts, settings.schema.json, opponent.schema.json) byte for byte with the committed packages/chess-ui/src/generated files and fails telling you to run `mise run generate:settings` when one is stale.

The e2e browser tests (marked e2e, run by `mise run test:e2e` which builds the web UI first) boot langgraph dev offline with stripped credentials and a replacement chess graph using a ScriptedModel and FakeRanker, drive Chromium via Playwright in desktop and phone contexts, and assert that setup settings reach the agent (stored setup, prompt, shortlist size) plus phone layout fit and tap sizes, moves by tap and drag, the reply card, promotion, resignation, FEN starts, and that a dropped first-move response is played only once.

langchain_chess_evals.testing provides fake_analysis, FakePool (stand-in for EnginePool), FakeFetch (in-memory URL fetcher) and FakeDatasetClient (in-memory slice of langsmith.Client for uploads and experiments), which the evals tests use instead of Stockfish, Lichess and LangSmith.

The evals live tests run the System 1 eval target with a real GatewayRanker (typesafe/jev-latest) on the starting position, expecting all 20 legal moves ranked with no tournament, and verify LangSmith enforces the positions dataset schemas with a throwaway dataset that is deleted afterwards.

The shared JS test setup adds jest-dom matchers, polyfills jsdom-missing layout/media APIs (matchMedia, scrollIntoView, pointer capture, ResizeObserver, requestAnimationFrame) and runs cleanup and clears localStorage after each test.

The e2e suite tests the web UI's sign-in banner without LangSmith by routing `**/assistants/search` to a 401 in Playwright and expecting 'Sign-in needed', and checks the Settings dialog reports that the e2e server needs no sign-in.

Server auth tests verify `user_for` with locally generated Ed25519 keys and EdDSA JWTs plus an injected signing-key lookup: a member of the configured app and org gets in as their `sub`, missing/non-bearer headers and unverifiable tokens (wrong signature, expired, wrong audience or issuer, no sub, garbage) are 401, a verified token from another app or org is 403, and a policy with either field unset refuses every token.

The registered `authenticate` handler is tested without contacting LangSmith by setting OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/ALLOWED_ORGANIZATION_ID, clearing the cached `_policy`, and monkeypatching the cached `_jwks` client with a hand-written FakeJwks that returns the test public key and records the looked-up token.

The web `Root` component takes `config`, `signIn`, `check`, `tab` and `local` as injectable props (defaulting to the build config, `makeSignIn`, a server access check and browser storages) so tests need no LangSmith or server; Root tests stub `App` and drive misconfiguration, no-sign-in, API-key sign-in/out and OAuth-button cases through these props.

The web auth tests use hand-written fakes for external boundaries: a fake oidc-client-ts manager with unsigned tokens carrying `organization_id` for `langsmithSignIn`, a fake `makeSignIn` returning scripted `Resumed` values plus an injected `check` for `useSession`, a fake fetcher for `checkAccess`, an explicit env object for `langsmithAppConfig`, and a storage that throws SecurityError for stored credentials.
